title: PCSS causes self-shadowing
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.6-dev5.
Reproducible in 4.0-stable.

### System information

Void #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Nov 14 02:05:35 UTC 2025 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970 (nvidia; 580.105.08) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-7600K CPU @ 3.80GHz (4 threads) - 15.50 GiB memory

### Issue description

I've been having issues with the `light_angular_distance` property on directional lights, which enables PCSS, and they seems to be related to the angle between the surface normal and the direction of the light, as well as the combined `light_angular_distance` + `shadow_blur`. It is very prominent on small objects, as the shadows cease to exist at all. I played with the biasing of the light and while it seemed to somewhat fix it, I could still find angles that made the shadow disappear.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9786c24-2405-4eee-a8fd-676135c9bbd7

With larger casters, it becomes apparent that the shadows disappear because they get much blurrier when parallel:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ec928bd-b6f6-4b83-96f0-91b2a4464575

There also seems to be some weird relation to the angle of the shadow receiver and the amount of blur that is applied:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0ea22a0-7942-44f2-ae44-dcd5a7ca45ce

If the receiver is close to parallel, then it basically has no blur. I'm pretty sure that this is not how this is supposed to work.

### Steps to reproduce

- Open mrp.
- Rotate plane.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[angular-distance_2025-12-13_00-06-08.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24140574/angular-distance_2025-12-13_00-06-08.zip)
